headline: South Asia: Houthi attacks on Saudi sites claim four more lives
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Houthi attacks on Saudi sites claim four more lives.
- Western Russia: Ukrainian forces strike Russian command post, drone launch site and warehouses.
- Persian Gulf Region: US-Iran war, then and now: How the landscape has changed since February.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: US Army long-range fires make a splash on the frontline with China.
- Military Times, one day ago: US Army long-range fires make a splash on the frontline with China.
The U.S. Army has been upgrading its missiles and rocket artillery, largely in response to China's missile arsenal.
- Military Times, 2 days ago: Navy offers explosive ordnance disposal warfare officers up to $100,000 in bonuses.
Eligable lieutenants and lieutenant commanders in the explosive ordnance disposal field are eligible for up to $100,000 in retention bonuses.
The Caribbean - bottom line: ‘You can’t just live for yourself’ - 88-y-o Merle Stern awarded for decades of community service.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 10 hours ago: ‘You can’t just live for yourself’ - 88-y-o Merle Stern awarded for decades of community service.
At 88, Merle Stern has little interest in measuring her life by the accolades she has racked up. For the retired justice of the peace, the greater reward has been the opportunity to help people through their difficulties, restore relationships, and ensure that the needs of the vulnerable are not overlooked.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA

Russian forces launched repeated drone strikes on Kharkiv, damaging residential buildings, a circus structure and cars and injuring a girl and a boy.

Russian forces attacked two private businesses in Chernihiv on 23 October, killing one person and injuring 25 others, local authorities reported.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Vessel presumably struck by drone sinks in Black Sea, one killed and three missing – video.
Romanian rescue vessels have pulled nine survivors and one deceased crew member from the Black Sea following a drone attack on the cargo ship Khoryv.

U.S. President Donald Trump has the world’s war crimes court in his crosshairs. By sanctioning the entire International Criminal Court, his administration is threatening its ability to function. Europe has rushed to the court’s defense — but can it actually protect it from American financial power? And how far is the European Union willing to […]

The leader of Ethiopia’s rebel Tigray People’s Liberation Front says the northern state is still at war. In a message aired on Tigrayan television on Wednesday, Debretsion Gebremichael said the TPLF is continuing to fight federal forces in the region and will “remain a graveyard for its enemies.”

South Asia - bottom line: Houthi attacks on Saudi sites claim four more lives.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 13 hours ago: Houthi attacks on Saudi sites claim four more lives.
• Rebels claim targeting Saudi defence ministry, Aramco installations, Dammam airport • Coalition downs four drones above Riyadh, Madina • Egypt urges talks as its parliament weighs military backing for Saudi campaign in Yemen • IRGC warns US against escorting ships thru Hormuz • Pakistan warns pilgrims travelling between Iran and Iraq RIYADH: Yemen’s Houthi forces said on Thursday they had launched attacks on Saudi Arabia’s defence ministry in Riyadh, Aramco facilities in Yanbu and the King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, where Saudi authorities said two people were killed.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 4 hours ago: 10 India-sponsored terrorists killed as bid to undermine state's writ in Gwadar foiled: ISPR.
Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Friday that 10 India-sponsored terrorists were killed in separate engagements as security forces thwarted their attempts to “undermine the writ of the state” in Balochistan’s Gwadar district.
- Dawn (Pakistan), South China Morning Post - China, The Hindu - International, Jerusalem Post, ABC News Australia, just now: West Bank attack wounds 5 Israelis as Netanyahu cancels events.
An attack in the occupied West Bank wounded at least five Israelis on Friday and triggered a shootout that left two Palestinians dead, prompting Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to cancel political events days ahead of elections. An AFP journalist who witnessed the firefight saw two Palestinian men in casual attire and armed with a handgun and an automatic rifle exchanging fire with Israeli forces at a checkpoint near the Palestinian city of Hebron. The journalist reported that Israeli forces eventually shot and killed the attackers.
- Dawn (Pakistan), just now: 'Will petrol be available in December?': Senate echoes with shortage concerns even as minister says no supply issues.
ISLAMABAD: The Senate echoed with fuel supply concerns on Friday as PPP’s Sherry Rehman questioned petrol availability for December and Opposition Leader Raja Nasir Abbas warned of a bleak situation amid heightening Middle East tensions. The concerns were raised even after Minister of State for Finance and Revenue Bilal Azhar Kayani said that there were no supply issues.
India - bottom line: Saudi Arabia eyes bigger missiles as Houthi threat meets Iran nuclear fears.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: Saudi Arabia eyes bigger missiles as Houthi threat meets Iran nuclear fears.
Recent reports indicate that Saudi Arabia is stepping up its missile production capabilities by developing a new missile complex near Al-Dawadmi. This initiative seems focused on creating solid-fuel missiles, potentially improving the kingdom's defense against threats, particularly from Yemen's Houthi movement. As these advancements unfold, fears about a possible nuclear arms race with Iran grow, especially with the US civilian nuclear cooperation agreement raising concerns over regional nuclear proliferation.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: Asian Para Games: Sumit Antil leads India's javelin 1-2-3; Pranav strikes gold again.
India's para-athletes had a remarkable performance at the Asian Para Games, securing two gold medals. Sumit Antil maintained his dominance in the men's javelin throw with a top distance of 72.46m, while Pranav Soorma broke records to defend his men's club throw F51 title. Complementing their achievements, Mahendra Gurjar earned silver, and Sandip Sanjay Sargar claimed bronze in javelin, boosting India's standing in the competition.

Japanese universities and other educational institutions more than doubled their applications for defence ministry research funding this year to a record 291, up from 123 last year, as Tokyo moves to strengthen its defences. The increase is the clearest sign yet that academia’s decades-long resistance to military-linked work is easing. Ukrainian police said on Friday they had detained a 17-year-old girl suspected of helping Russia’s security services to poison Ukrainian soldiers and that two had died. Ukraine and Russia have throughout their war since 2022 accused each other of recruiting minors for sabotage acts including poisoning. AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Threats against politicians are on the rise. How can we move to a better, safer politics?.
- The Guardian - Australia, one hour ago: Threats against politicians are on the rise. How can we move to a better, safer politics?.
The alleged attack on independent MP Helen Haines has horrified Australia. But around the world, politicians and women in particular face increased threats to their safety “Thoughts and prayers.” After each soul-destroying mass shooting in the United States, this is the platitude invariably trotted out by every impotent politician unable to confront the stranglehold reality of the country’s gun lobby. “Turn the temperature down,” risks becoming Australia’s equivalent.

In the wake of the attack on Helen Haines, several NSW politicians speak about being subjected to threats of violence.
- The Guardian - Australia, one hour ago: Do leaders lack the courage to turn the temperature down? – podcast.
Tony Barry and George Megalogenis (filling in for Barrie Cassidy) examine the response to the horrific alleged attack on independent MP Helen Haines this week. While the prime minister pleaded for all to ‘turn the temperature’ down, it didn’t take long for many to dial it right up, particularly online. So can politicians from all sides tell their tribes to tone down the rhetoric? And what lessons can we learn from history to help us all navigate toxic public debate?
